truths.truth: From an empty home, terminus creates its data directory and database owner-only, and doctor reports no failure caused by the fresh state
truths.evidence: Ran under env -i with HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME in an empty scratch dir. Before any ingest, doctor reported data_directory, store and last_run as note/unknown (not problem); its 6 problems were the binary, four hooks and mcp_server not being installed, each with an install fix. After `terminus ingest` (exit 0): xdg/terminus 700, terminus.db 600, LOCK 600, snapshots/ 700 and its snapshot 600; doctor then showed data_directory, store and last_run ok. In a second scratch home after `terminus install --yes`, doctor printed 'no problems.' and exited 0.

PROJECT.md names it at :21 and :106 and :131 (each says removed) and at :35 and :55 (shipped-cycle Manifest rows). truths.truth: No Windows or Unix guard, Windows variable or .exe literal is left in crates/
truths.evidence: The AC2 pattern returned rc=1 (no match) both from `git grep -nE` over crates and from `grep -rnE` over the working tree. `git grep target_os -- crates` shows only lib.rs:22 (the refusal), config.rs:928/933 (macOS and Linux fold), store/open.rs:855/869 (Linux and macOS data dir), and the cfg!(target_os = "macos") arms in tests/datamove.rs:71 and tests/owner_only.rs:81. No match for cfg(.*windows, windows_sys, std::os::windows, creation_flags or target_family. Remaining 'windows' words in crates are .windows( slice calls, blob.rs block windows, show.rs variables, or comments the plans kept on purpose: claude-mem history (project.rs:182, doctor.rs:1208, targets.rs:27-29), Claude Code behaviour (doctor.rs:446) and transcript data (egress.rs:423, json.rs:152).

truths.truth: lib.rs carries the guarded compile_error! and a test fails if the guard or message is removed
truths.evidence: crates/terminus-core/src/lib.rs:22-23 has `#[cfg(not(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "macos")))]` followed by `compile_error!("Terminus supports Linux and macOS only.");`, before the first `pub mod` at :25. crates/terminus-core/tests/supported_systems.rs::a_build_for_any_other_system_stops_at_compile_time passed in the full suite. Mutation check, compiled standalone with rustc --test against scratch copies of lib.rs: the original passes; the guard changed to not(unix) FAILS ('lib.rs has no line #[cfg(not(any(...)))]'); one word of the message changed FAILS ('lib.rs has no line compile_error!(...)'); both lines deleted FAILS.

truths.truth: A Windows cargo build fails with 'Terminus supports Linux and macOS only.'
truths.evidence: Not runnable here: `rustup target list --installed` shows only x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and there is no x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc. Installing a target would need the network. The guard is present and pinned (truth 4), but whether MSVC shows the message before or among the unresolved std::os::unix errors is CONTEXT's first flagged assumption and is unobserved.

truths.truth: The full suite passes at the stated count and the summary lists every test helper and .exe arm removed
truths.evidence: One run of `cargo test --workspace --all-features` at 100a1ec exited 0: 750 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. `-- --list` counts 750 `: test` lines. That is the 749 baseline plus the AC3 refusal test. `git diff 26b79d1 HEAD -- crates` adds exactly one #[test] line and removes none (the source count is 750 to 751 because corpus.rs:375 names #[test] in a doc comment). AC5's literal '749' no longer matches; CONTEXT's third flagged assumption says a moved count is accounted for in the summary, SUMMARY.md:28 does that, and issue #6 tracks the wording. Every non-comment line removed from tests is a cfg guard, one of the two `#[cfg(not(unix))] fn drain` stubs, one of the four terminus.exe arms (doctor, hook, install, uninstall), the datamove LOCALAPPDATA env line and Windows data_dir arm, one of the four USERPROFILE lines, or the `del` disjunct. This matches SUMMARY.md:20-26 item for item. `git grep -nw 'fn drain'` shows corpus.rs:560 and hook.rs:359 only.

truths.truth: doctor, doctor --json and uninstall print no attrib, del or .exe fix and no mention of Windows, and doctor --json keeps its top-level keys
truths.evidence: In a scratch home (env -i, HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME in scratch) I ran install --yes, doctor, doctor --json, uninstall --yes and install over a stranger at the stable path. `grep -i -E 'attrib|\bdel |\.exe\b|windows'` over all of that output found nothing (rc=1). With the data dir made read-only, doctor's fix was `chmod u+w '<dir>'`. The occupied-path refusal prints `rm -f '<path>' && ... install`. In the source diff 26b79d1..HEAD, doctor.rs drops only the claude.exe, attrib and del branches (no check added or removed), install/mod.rs::occupied drops only the del branch, and uninstall.rs::unplace drops only the 'on Windows it can only be removed after this process exits' block. doctor --json envelope keys are [command, data, ok, reason], pinned by tests/doctor.rs::the_json_document_carries_every_check_by_name, which passed. The data keys are the 14 check names, and none changed.

gaps.missing: The owner decides which way to settle it. One option is to amend ROADMAP SC5's doctor clause to what D-12 delivers (doctor prints only Unix fixes and no Windows text). The other is to have doctor state the supported systems, which adds a check name to --json data but leaves the envelope keys AC6 pins unchanged. Issue #7 already tracks it.

human_checks.name: On a Windows machine with Rust installed, run `cargo build` in the Terminus repository root
human_checks.expected: The build fails, and its output contains "Terminus supports Linux and macOS only." It should appear first or at least among the unresolved std::os::unix errors.
human_checks.why_human: Out-of-reach resource. This machine has only the x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu std (rustup target list --installed) and no x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc. Adding a Windows target needs the network, and a cross-build also needs a C compiler for the bundled SQLite and zstd. The source-scan test proves the guard is present, but only a real Windows build shows the message is reached (CONTEXT's first flagged assumption).
